questions.question: Describe the four main elements of weather.
questions.expected_answer: Temperature is how hot or cold the air is, measured in degrees Celsius. Wind is moving air, described by its strength and the direction it comes from. Cloud cover is how much of the sky is covered by cloud, from clear to overcast. Precipitation is water falling from clouds as rain, hail or snow.

questions.question: Explain how clouds form.
questions.expected_answer: Warm, moist air rises. As it rises, it cools, and the invisible water vapour in it turns into billions of tiny drops of water or bits of ice, which float together as a cloud.

questions.question: Explain the difference between rain, hail and snow.
questions.expected_answer: Rain is drops of liquid water. Hail is balls of ice that form inside tall thunderclouds, where winds carry drops up into freezing air again and again, building up layers of ice. Snow is ice crystals that stay frozen all the way to the ground, falling mainly on high mountains in winter.
